messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposal is to treat large refactors as an "interleaving cutover" instead of a big-bang. goal: safe parallel work + bounded tech-debt escrow. want feedback on guardrails.
ben: sounds promising. can you sketch the lifecycle of a unit of work in the escrow?
sanjay: +1 on avoiding big-bang. curious about tenant isolation during cutover — do we need per-tenant feature flags?
maria: yep, per-tenant flags + traffic routing. lifecycle: 1) create adapter in new slice behind flag, 2) route small percent of traffic, 3) automatic observability checks, 4) promote or rollback, 5) schedule debt-paydown tasks for leftover behavior.
alex: how do we keep the backlog bounded? open to a ticketing rule or SLA on escrow time?
maria: propose 'debt escrow' queue with max age 30d and ownership handoff required at 2w. owners must either resolve, defer with justification, or fund an engineering slot.
karen: can we codify the guardrails into a lightweight policy config? example: 
```
cutover_policy:
  max_escrow_days: 30
  review_deadline_days: 14
  observability_gates:
    - p50_latency_delta: 10%
    - error_rate_delta: 0.5%
  canary_percentages: [1, 5, 20]
```
ben: nice. what signals do we need to auto-fail a promotion? p95 > baseline by X? error rate spike?
sanjay: also watch for cache-hit regressions and KV cache miss tail. those kill cost.
maria: yes — baseline p95, error rate, and cache-hit ratio. autoscale & ephemeral rollout if any gate fails. we should require at least two consecutive canary windows passing.
akex: typo: alex: will we need feature-flag infra changes (flags-as-code) to manage per-tenant?
maria: prefer flags-as-code + tag them with migration-id so we can query outstanding migrations easily.
karen: note on product: some tenants can't be cutover until compliance signoff. the policy must allow manual hold.
ben: who owns the escrow queue? infra team or the service team?
sanjay: I'd argue service team owns the migration change; infra owns the routing & tooling. backgrounds ops to ensure no orphaned items.
maria: agreed. owner metadata required on escrow items: migration-id, owner, ticket-link, estimated-effort.
alex: can we add a quick CLI to inspect escrow items? e.g., `ri esc list --stale`
maria: yep, add to eng-toolbelt.
karen: rollout cadence question — do we force one migration per sprint or allow multiple?
sanjay: allow multiple but cap concurrent migrations per runtime node to avoid resource contention. cap = 3 per node as starting point.
ben: dependency graph problem: if migration B depends on A, we need blocking semantics and avoids partial exposure.
maria: propose adding `depends_on` field and de-prioritizing dependents until parents pass. also add a small graph check to the CI.
alex: how do we measure paydown throughput? metric ideas: escrow_count, avg_time_in_escrow, resolved_per_week.
karen: product will care about number of outstanding migrations for their adoption report. include a dashboard.
maria: implementation plan: week1 prototyping: escrow datastore + minimal UI, flags-as-code tagging, CLI. week2: implement observability gates & canary runner. week3: soft rollout on non-critical service, iterate.
sanjay: rollback story? we should document automatic rollback + manual rollback runbook. include steps to flush KV cache to avoid inconsistent reads.
b​en: small nit — flushing cache on rollback can be noisy; consider targeted invalidation by migration tag.
maria: good call. we'll add targeted invalidation.
deploy-bot: Canary started for migration-id=mig-2026-042; 1% traffic -> service-b-new. logs: https://ci.internal/1234
alex: saw the canary. error-rate slight blip at +0.2% but within gate. monitoring looks ok. :thumbsup:
karen: let's hold manual signoff for tenants with compliance flag. maria can you add the hold list to the dashboard?
maria: will do. assigning initial implementation to @sanjay for escrow store + @alex for CLI and @ben for dashboard widgets.
sanjay: got it. will open tracker tickets today.
ben: adding dashboard widgets ticket now.
maria: thanks — follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30. if anyone has immediate blockers shout here. :coffee:
